english: The number of functions $f:\{1,2,3,4\}\to\{1,2,3\}$ whose range contains both 1 and 2 is ______.
solution: All functions: $3^{4}=81$; range misses 1: $2^{4}=16$; misses 2: $16$; misses both: $1^{4}=1$
solution_full: There are $3^{4}=81$ functions from a 4-element set to a 3-element set.

Let $P$ be the set of functions whose range does not contain 1 and $Q$ the set whose range does not contain 2. A function in $P$ maps into $\{2,3\}$: $|P|=2^{4}=16$; likewise $|Q|=16$; and $|P\cap Q|=1$ (the constant function 3).
By inclusion-exclusion, the functions whose range contains both 1 and 2 number $81-(16+16-1)=50$.
Check: such a range is $\{1,2\}$ or $\{1,2,3\}$. Onto functions to $\{1,2,3\}$: $3^{4}-3\cdot2^{4}+3\cdot1^{4}=36$; functions with range exactly $\{1,2\}$: $2^{4}-2=14$; total $50$.
originality_note: New: functions whose range must contain a given part of the codomain, which is an onto-type inclusion-exclusion over only the required values (way 5). Closest known: number of onto functions from a 4-set to a 3-set (36). Different because: the free value 3 changes the alternating sum, and the onto count appears only as a check.

concept_use.Number of onto (surjective) functions vi: The onto count 3^4 - 3.2^4 + 3 = 36 is the check (range exactly {1,2,3}); the main count is its partial version.
